en.headline: Four franchised bus operators apply for fare rises of up to 17.7 per cent
en.dek: Citybus seeks the largest increase amid higher fuel costs, with the government to review applications at a Legislative Council panel on Friday.
body: Four Hong Kong franchised bus operators have applied for fare increases ranging from 8.1 to 17.7 per cent, citing significant financial pressure from soaring diesel prices linked to the Middle East conflict, the Transport and Logistics Bureau said.

Citybus has requested 17.7 per cent, Kowloon Motor Bus 16 per cent, New Lantao Bus 9.8 per cent and Long Win Bus 8.1 per cent. The applications, submitted in April, will be discussed at the Legislative Council Transport Panel on Friday before going to the Chief Executive in Council for a final decision.

Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan said the government would carefully balance service reliability, the operators’ financial sustainability and public affordability, reviewing a full basket of factors including cost and revenue forecasts and the impact on passengers. The last approved rises for several operators took effect in January 2025.

zh.headline: 四間專營巴士營辦商申請加價 加幅8.1%至17.7%
zh.dek: 城巴申請最高17.7%，九巴16%，政府將於星期五立法會交通事務委員會討論，強調會平衡營運可持續性與市民負擔能力。
body: 運輸及物流局表示，四間專營巴士營辦商已提交加價申請，加幅由8.1%至17.7%不等，主要因中東衝突導致柴油價格急升，構成重大財政壓力。
城巴申請加價17.7%，九巴16%，嶼巴9.8%，龍運8.1%。申請於今年4月提交，立法會交通事務委員會將於星期五討論，其後交由行政長官會同行政會議最終決定。
運輸及物流局局長陳美寶指，政府會審慎考慮一籃子因素，包括營辦商營運情況、成本收入預測及對市民的影響，重視服務可靠性與財務可持續性，同時顧及公眾負擔能力。上一次批准的加價於2025年1月生效。
